content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm interested in knowing if it's possible to combine the [product_name] [version_no] [article_no] with the expansion module [version_no] [article_no]. I require some relay outputs and some standard outputs, so this setup seems ideal since it would provide plenty of inputs and the necessary outputs. Thank you,
Hello [user_name], Here is a link to the manual: [url] Refer to chapter 2 for further details. Best regards,
Yes, it's possible. However, you need a [product_name] [version_no] expansion unit with the correct [article_no]. The right model number should end with 2, not 0 or 1.
Thank you for your quick and helpful response!
Hi all, Additionally, here is an overview of compatibility between [product_name] basic and expansion modules. Best regards,

In my opinion, both modules are compatible, since their supply voltage is the same. Please review the manual first. If the expansion module is compatible with your [product_name], it will attach to the right side of your module. If you already have it, there's no need to worry. If you're purchasing, consult your local distributor regarding compatibility. Hope this helps.
Extension modules are always connected on the right side. That's been the design from the beginning.
If the expansion module has a different supply voltage, you won't be able to attach both together because their assembly design is not compatible. Make sure to test before answering.
Introducing different voltage classes here is unnecessary. The initial question was strictly about 24VDC for both the basic and expansion modules. Bringing up other voltages isn't helpful.
[article_no] is a basic module for 12/24VDC, so it works on 24VDC. The expansion module [article_no] is for 24VDC. Therefore, both modules operate with the same voltage.

Hi, I have the same PLC and DI/DO module ([article_no]-PLC, [article_no]-module (relay)), and I haven't encountered any issues connecting them. Additionally, connecting the analog input module [article_no] also works without a problem. So, what [user_name] stated is correct.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focused on the compatibility of [product_name] basic and expansion modules, specifically regarding certain [article_no] units and their ability to be combined for the required input/output configurations. Main insights underline the need to match supply voltages and correct module versions. After clarifying some confusion about voltage, users agreed that 24VDC modules are compatible, confirming the initial setup meets user needs.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to expand their [product_name] system efficiently by combining basic and expansion modules to achieve the needed types and numbers of inputs and outputs, without experiencing compatibility problems.
